result.rationale: CleanCapital is one active U.S. solar-and-storage platform. BlackRock funds invested directly in the firm in 2019, but the 2021 Manulife transaction restructured CleanCapital around its balance sheet and ended BlackRock's ownership of the original 46.9 MW asset partnership. Current company materials name Manulife as the backer. No evidence shows GIP directly owned CleanCapital or received the investment when BlackRock acquired GIP.

identityResolution.boundary: Include the manager-level owner/operator/developer. Exclude project SPVs, financing vehicles and integrated subsidiary BQ Energy as separate PortCos.

owners.vehicle: John Hancock Life Insurance Company (U.S.A.) balance sheet and third-party managed accounts
owners.transactionState: CURRENT; commitment increased in 2023 and Manulife plus unnamed co-investors added $145 million of equity in 2024
FORMER_DIRECT_EQUITY; exact platform-level exit mechanics and date are undisclosed

ownershipResolution.BlackRock: Preserve the 2019 historical period; retire current status and remove the unsupported Evergreen Infrastructure Fund attribution.
ownershipResolution.GlobalInfrastructurePartners: No ownership period. BlackRock's 2024 manager-level acquisition of GIP does not prove a legal transfer of CleanCapital.
ownershipResolution.current: Manulife is the only named current institutional backer; 2024 co-investors were unnamed.

operatingResolution.sector: Distributed solar and energy storage infrastructure
operatingResolution.model: Develops, builds, owns, operates and invests in contracted distributed-energy assets.
operatingResolution.footprint: United States; current materials report activity across 30 states and U.S. territories.
operatingResolution.scale: January 2026: over 350 projects and 500 MW. Current site: over 450 MW managed, over 1 GW in development and over $1.5 billion invested.

acquisitionExitCheck.platformResult: No public platform sale, merger, bankruptcy or signed pending exit found.
acquisitionExitCheck.assetResult: CleanCapital completed the 120 MW Nottingham development sale to Energix on 2026-04-22; this was an asset sale, not a platform exit.

milestones.event: BlackRock Renewable Power Group funds invested directly in CleanCapital.
Manulife made a corporate investment and $300 million commitment; CleanCapital became sole owner of the 46.9 MW portfolio previously financed with BlackRock.
Manulife and institutional co-investors added $145 million of equity.
CleanCapital completed the Nottingham project sale to Energix; asset-level only.
